obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N71-R04)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data in the merchant CDE, including a common point of purchase notice
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (merchant agreement term)
notify: Acquiring bank merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - merchant role (contract, not law)
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 - card brand rule applied through the acquirer, not law
trigger: Discovery of evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes, or transmits it
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (North America), through or alongside the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - as a Level 1 merchant and as a service provider (Section A applies to any entity, including service providers)
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa; include containment and remediation steps with dates and supporting PCI DSS documentation when available or requested
notify: Visa and the acquiring bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise event
deadline: Immediately
notify: Issuing or acquiring bank; Visa recommends also notifying legal, the POS or shopping cart vendor if a vulnerability is involved, and law enforcement (U.S. Secret Service in the United States)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days, uploaded through the acquirer or processor
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (through the acquirer or processor)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the payment service and processors can list card numbers authorized during the window of exposure
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Visa: PCI forensic investigation (if Visa requires it)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Formal notice from Visa that a PFI is required (more likely for Level 1 merchants and service providers, Section A.5.2)
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; initial forensic report within 5 business days of signing; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation. The PFI must not have provided services (including QSA work) to the company in the past 3 years
notify: Visa and affected acquirers (the PFI reports directly to Visa)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if required; the company's current QSA firm is not eligible
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Visa: independent investigation (if Visa requires it instead)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.6
trigger: Formal notice from Visa that an independent investigation is required
deadline: Contract a qualified investigator within 5 business days; contain the event within 60 business days or Visa may require a PFI
notify: Visa (reports go directly from the investigator)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if required
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

citation: Mastercard, American Express, and Discover operating rules - applied through the acquirer, not law
trigger: Suspected compromise of those brands' card data
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified here)
notify: Acquirer; card brands through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; these rules were not verified
owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Client merchant notice (SL-1 service provider role)
citation: SL-1 client agreements (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirements 12.9 and 12.10.1 (N71-R04)
trigger: Suspected compromise affecting a client's checkout, card data, or patron data
deadline: Within 72 hours of suspicion (client agreement term); clients then notify their own acquirers
notify: Each affected client's designated security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - service provider role (contract, not law)

trigger: The company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination (made without unreasonable delay after discovery)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05: Attorney General delay
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Attorney General delay); SEC Release 33-11216
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Filing delayed for the period the Attorney General specifies
notify: SEC (through the Department of Justice)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely; counsel decides whether to request it

trigger: Information required by Item 1.05 was not determined or was unavailable at the time of the initial filing
deadline: Identify the missing information in the initial filing and file an amended Form 8-K when it is determined or becomes available, as the release describes
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the Form 10-K; describe material effects of incidents under 106(b)(2)
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - patrons in all 50 states; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
clock_starts: Varies by state (often discovery or determination of the breach)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a card number and any required security code, an email address with a password, and information about geolocation (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 more days if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); the extension applies only to this notice to individuals
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - as covered entity for the company's own patrons; for client checkouts the client is the covered entity and the company is its third-party agent
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity (outbound)
trigger: Breach of a system the company maintains as a third-party agent for a client venue (client checkout or client patron data)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; provide the client all information it needs to give its notices. The company may give notices on the client's behalf (501.171(6)(b))
notify: Each affected client venue (covered entity)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SL-1 client checkouts; the 72-hour contract term comes first
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor (for example the tag vendor or the outsourced contact center) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: No later than 10 days following the vendor's determination; the company then gives the notices above
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - also add 72-hour contract terms (POAM-009)

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice to individuals would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination in writing, keep it 5 years, and provide it to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides for other data

citation: n/a (voluntary); Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3.3.4 recommends notifying law enforcement
trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card or patron data
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0 to 2)
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office or FBI (IC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering an extortion payment (for example a demand not to publish the patron export)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability

trigger: Incident affecting a managed venue's systems, settlement data, or patrons
deadline: Within 72 hours of suspicion (agreement term)
notify: Owner's designated contact
applies_at_this_tier: Only if SL-2 systems or data are affected
owner: Senior Vice President, Venue Management Services

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope includes entities in a critical infrastructure sector above the SBA size standard; the company is above its standard

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a Nevada gaming licensee
deadline: Notify the Chair within 24 hours of activating the incident response plan; Initial Cybersecurity Incident Response report within 5 calendar days; written updates every 30 days; investigation report available on request
notify: Chair of the Nevada Gaming Control Board
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no gaming license and has no Nevada venues (N71-R01)

trigger: Suspicious activity at a casino or card club
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection of facts that may be a basis for filing
notify: FinCEN
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a casino or card club (N71-R03)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
